question.text: A uniform horizontal rod OA, of mass 4 kg and length 2 m, is hinged to a wall at end O. A massless string AB supports end A, where B is a point on the wall above O; the string meets the rod at A making an angle of 60° with the rod. Taking g = 10 m/s², work out the following.

parts.label: a
parts.asks: Determine the tension in the string AB.

parts.label: b
parts.asks: Determine the net force the hinge exerts on the rod at O.

conditions: rod OA is horizontal and uniform, mass 4 kg, length 2 m
hinged to a vertical wall at O
string AB attached at A, wall point B above O
string AB makes 60° with the rod at A

figure.description: A vertical wall on the left with a rod OA hinged at O, extending horizontally to the right to end A, length 2 m. A string runs from A up to a point B on the wall, above O, making a 60° angle with the rod at A.

solution.approach: Take torques about the hinge to find the string tension, then balance forces on the rod to find the hinge force.

steps.text: The rod's weight acts at its center, 1 m from the hinge; the string's vertical part acts at the far end, 2 m from the hinge.
Balance the horizontal and vertical forces on the rod to find the two parts of the hinge force.
steps.equation: H_x = T cos60° ≈ 11.55 N, H_y = mg − T sin60° = 20 N

steps.text: Combine the two parts to get the size of the net hinge force.

final_answer.value: (a) T ≈ 23.09 N, (b) net hinge force ≈ 23.09 N

common_mistakes.text: Using the rod's full length, 2 m, as the weight's distance from the hinge instead of 1 m gives T ≈ 46.19 N, twice the correct value.
